claim.quote: An excess over known backgrounds is observed at low energies and most prominent between 2 and 3 keV.

date.note: 2020-06 derived from the arXiv identifier 2006.09721 (YYMM prefix = 2020-06); exact day not confirmed by a fetched source. Journal publication was later in 2020 (Phys. Rev. D 102, 072004).

key_value_text.quote: the excess favors a monoenergetic peak at (2.3+-0.2) keV (68% C.L.) with a 3.0 sigma global (4.0 sigma local) significance
key_value_text.value: Excess most prominent between 2 and 3 keV; if interpreted as a monoenergetic peak, centered at (2.3+-0.2) keV with 3.0 sigma global (4.0 sigma local) significance -- interpretation unconfirmed.

name: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T
notes: This is explicitly NOT a discovery, observation, or confirmed dark-matter signal: the collaboration's own abstract frames every explanation (axion, neutrino magnetic moment, tritium, bosonic dark matter) as a hypothesis with no interpretation confirmed or excluded.

significance.quote: The solar axion model has a 3.4 sigma significance ... The significances of the solar axion and neutrino magnetic moment hypotheses are reduced to 2.0 sigma and 0.9 sigma, respectively, if an unconstrained tritium component is included in the fitting.
significance.value: up to 3.4 sigma (solar axion hypothesis, before tritium is allowed to float; reduces to 2.0 sigma if an unconstrained tritium component is included)

summary.plain: In 2020, XENON1T reported seeing more low-energy electron-recoil events than expected. The excess was never confirmed as dark matter, a new particle or any other specific cause -- possible explanations included a tiny amount of natural radioactivity (tritium) in the detector, solar particles called axions, or a new neutrino property -- and it remains an open, unresolved anomaly.
summary.technical: XENON1T low-energy (1-30 keV) electronic-recoil search, 0.65 t-y exposure, background rate 76+-2 events/(t y keV). An excess above background is observed, most prominent between 2 and 3 keV. Solar axion (3.4 sigma), enhanced neutrino magnetic moment (3.2 sigma) and tritium beta-decay (3.2 sigma) hypotheses were tested; a bosonic-dark-matter interpretation favors a peak at (2.3+-0.2) keV at 3.0 sigma global / 4.0 sigma local significance. None of these is confirmed; the collaboration's own paper treats it as an open excess, not a discovery.

title: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T
why_it_matters: The most-discussed unexplained anomaly in the direct-detection field this decade; it motivated dedicated follow-up analyses by XENONnT and other experiments and is still not resolved.
